REGIS REPORT

13 August 2025

More 2Q25 results comments today for AP, BLOOM, CNVRG, FGEN, GTCAP, and PLDT. Apart from those, we have bits and bobs on CNPF, bank NPLs, fintech, DMCI, gaming, SM Prime, etc.

 

  • Aboitiz Power (AP PM) (-) – Weaker spot prices dragged AP’s 2Q25 performance, with beneficial EBITDA falling 4% YoY (+27% QoQ) to P19.1bn, bringing 1H25 EBITDA down 6% to P34.1bn. 1H25 profit of P12.7bn was lower by 26% YoY and trails consensus estimates, even with incremental earnings from Chromite and new solar additions.  That said, management expressed confidence for 2H, citing reduced spot exposure, higher hydro tariffs, and other positives. 

 

  • Bloomberry Resorts (BLOOM PM) (-) – The company recorded a net loss of P1.4bn in 2Q25, from recurring profit of P460mn in 1Q25. 2Q25 EBITDA fell 42% QoQ and 30% YoY to P2.5bn, behind REGIS and consensus forecasts. The decline was led by Solaire Entertainment City, which saw a 20% QoQ and 27% YoY decline in GGR (P9.8bn) as volumes of every category fell on a QoQ and YoY basis.

 

  • Converge (CNVRG) (=) – NPAT was up 12% YoY to P5.9bn, broadly in line with Street estimates. However, we note that 2Q profit slowed to P2.9bn up 7% YoY. Revenue growth also slowed to 10% YoY in 2Q (was 12% for 1H). Management has reduced its guidance for FY25 revenue growth to 10-12%, down from 14-6% previously.

 

  • First Gen (FGEN PM)(=) – Headline profit was US$162m (+5% YoY) in 1H, with recurring profit at US$151m (+1%). Profits from its natgas businesses was flat at US%72m.  Contributions from its geothermal business EDC declined 23% to US$34m, but the hydro business delivered US$15m (up 3x).  FGEN will see a major shift in its operations with the impending sale of 60% of its natgas business to Prime Infra.

 

  • GT Capital (GTCAP PM) (+) – GT Capital reported 1H25 net profit of P18.4bn (+34%) and core profit of P18.1bn (+31%), on pace to beat both Regis (P29bn) and Street (P31bn) estimates.  Toyota Motor Philippines (TMP) delivered robust numbers, with 1H25 profit up 66% YoY to P12.5bn (Ahead). Even though we anecdotally saw heavy promotional activities in 2Q, TMP’s EBIT margins positively surprised, as it was sustained at 12%-ish levels in 2Q/1H25, with GPMs further strengthening to a new high of 17.5% in 2Q25 (vs. 16.8% in 1Q25 and 13.6% in 2Q24). Management is holding a briefing this afternoon (2:30PM, registration).

 

  • PLDT (TEL PM) (=) – Core income for PLDT in 1H inched up +1% to P17.6bn, notwithstanding the decline (-2%) in mobile revenue.  PLDT was able to reduce cash opex (-3%) and also raised “wholesale international voice” revenues.  The accelerated asset write-downs and depreciation of prior years also helped limit ongoing depreciation costs. Maya, its fintech arm, also contributed P406m in core income in 1H25.

For Philippine-based investors>>PLDT - 2Q25: Mobile revenues remain weak

 

+ + +

 

Century Pacific (CNPF PM) is acquiring Loma Linda in the US to expand its alt-meat product range. While some may be wary of the segment, it’s useful to note that CNPF is only spending less than $10mn for the purchase, as the parent Atlantic Natural Foods (ANF) has filed for Chapter 11 in the US. CNPF already has its own alt-meat offering UnMeat, which is carried by Walmart. UnMeat is canned and shelf-stable, making it more popular (and cheaper) than frozen rivals.

 

Alliance Global’s (AGI) gaming arm Travellers is taking a majority stake in the Westside City integrated resort casino from SunTrust (SUN PM). The project is halfway through completion (target 3Q26), and will have 280 tables and 1,260 machines, adding roughly 20% to industry capacity in the Entertainment City area.

 

Banking sector NPLs were down 2bps MoM to 3.56% in June, while Past Due rates inched up 3bps to 4.50%. That said, the stable asset quality numbers give no hint to the new NPL formation data. Provision expense in 2Q26 jumped QoQ and YoY for nearly all banks that have reported. To be fair, this was due to the rapid expansion into consumer loans, which (for now) seem to still be generating better risk-adjusted returns despite the higher credit costs.

 

The BSP has cleared the way for the entry of Apple Pay and Google Pay in the Philippines. While this will not necessarily add new products, it could still improve adoption given the convenience of NFC tap-to-pay straight from your phone, without having to open the different bank or e-wallet apps. This would be particularly useful for public transportation, where transaction speed would be crucial.

POWER
Aboitiz Power: 2Q25 EBITDA declines 4% YoY on lower spot prices
  • 1H25 profit of P12.7bn (-26% YoY) lags consensus estimates. AP’s 1H25 net income fell 26% YoY to P12.7bn, weighed down by (a) the timing of planned outages (largely in 1Q25), (b) lower spot prices, (c) the recognition of non-cash and financing costs for GNPD, and (d) higher financing expenses arising from the acquisition of Chromite (i.e. natgas assets).  The profit decline was partly cushioned by contributions from Chromite, as well as new solar plants (377 MWp). The results appear to lag consensus’ full-year estimate of P32.9bn.

 

  • Generation 2Q25 EBITDA down 4% YoY due to steep drop in spot prices. Although AP reduced its WESM exposure to 17% in 2Q25 from ~30% in 1Q25/2Q24, EBITDA for the generation/RES segment still fell 4% YoY to P19.1bn in 2Q25 (+27% QoQ). Management blamed this on the steep decline in WESM prices, which more than offset gains from lower fuel costs. Given management’s subdued near- to medium-term outlook for spot prices, it has locked in close to 90% of its baseload capacity under long-term contracts over the next quarters.

 

  • Better 2H25 outlook. Management expects the sequential momentum in profit gains to carry into 2H, supported by (a) stable plant availability, (b) reduced spot exposure, (c) the full ramp-up of Excellent Energy under Chromite, and (d) the positive impact of the higher ancillary tariffs for some of its hydros, which were granted in July.   

 

  • Leverage up due to M&A. Following the acquisition of Chromite, AP’s net debt stood at P239bn in end-June, with net debt-to-equity jumping to 1.17x from 0.84x in end-2024.  Management refrained from discussing its victory in the auction for the 797MW Caliraya-Botocan-Kalayaan (CBK) hydro plant complex. Recall that AP, together Sumitomo Corp. and Electric Power Development Co., (a.k.a. “Thunder consortium”) submitted the highest bid of P36.3bn for CBK last month.

POWER
First Gen 2Q25 core profit rebounds, lifted by strong hydro performance
  • Headline 1H25 profit was up 5% YoY to US$162mn
    • On a recurring basis, profit stood at US$151mn in 1H25, up 1% YoY
    • 1H core profit represented 53% of consensus’ full-year estimate of US$287mn and REGIS’ FY25E of US$285mn
  • In 2Q25 alone, core profit rose 7% YoY to US$73.5mn, boosted by higher output at its hydro platform
  • Derived 2Q25 recurring contributions from its natgas unit (including LNG terminal) stood at US$72mn (flat)
    • Lower WESM prices affected San Gabriel’s performance but contributions from other natgas facilities and the LNG terminal compensated
  • EDC’s (ex-hydro) attributable recurring income stood at US$34mn (-23% YoY) in 1H25
    • Implied 2Q25 profit contribution from EDC was down 22% YoY to US$14mn
    • Cited lower sales and operating income due to lower electricity prices, higher interest expenses from new debt for expansions
  • Hydro unit contributed US$15mn in 1H25 (vs. US$5mn in 1H24)
    • Of which Pantabangan-Masiway (132MW) contributed US$13mn (vs. US$4mn) while Casecnan (165MW) contributed US$2mn (took over in Feb 26, 2024)
    • Higher water levels resulted in higher power output, higher sales to reserve market, and higher power supply contracts

 

 

CONSUMER
CNPF acquires Loma Linda to expand its plant-based offerings
  • Century Pacific North American, Inc. (CPNA), US-based subsidiary of Century Pacific Food, Inc. (CNPF PM) has acquired the Loma Linda brand from Atlantic Natural Foods, Inc. (ANF) for less than US$10mn to scale its plant-based offerings
  • The deal includes other brands such as Tuno, neat, Kaffree Roma, formulations, some manufacturing assets, licenses, remaining inventory of ANF
    • Products of Loma Linda vary from plant-based alternatives for tuna, chicken, and hotdogs, vegan/gluten free egg substitute, vegan coffee, among others sold across North America and 30 countries globally
  • ANF filed for Chapter 11 Bankruptcy back in April 2025, citing financial struggles from supply chain disruptions, inflation, US tariffs on steel used in its cans
    • The company's assets went up for bidding last July and CNPF emerging as the confirmed buyer
  • The transaction is expected to be immediately accretive as operational integration is seen to be a "bolt-on match" to CPNA's existing plant-based food operations (unMeat)
    • Prior to the acquisition, ANF was already a customer for CNPF's OEM business
  • ANF Vice President for Special Markets Jonathan Hines stated that ANF has already been using CNPF's production facility in the Philippines for the past six months
    • Hines emphasized that US distribution will remain intact but hinted that production will likely shift to the Philippines
  • In 2024, Milk & Others (which includes meat alternatives) was 29% of consolidated revenues, up from 24% back in 2020
GAMING
Travellers will reportedly take over Westside City integrated resort project
  • According to Inside Asian Gaming, Alliance Global’s Travellers will take over the Westside City integrated resort (IR) project from Suntrust Resort Holdings (SUN PM)
  • Travellers will have a majority stake in the project while Suntrust will have a minority stake
  • Suntrust Resort Holdings, which is controlled by the LET Group, has spent c. US$700mn out of the US$1.25bn construction cost for the project
  • Completion of the IR was previously moved from 4Q25 to 3Q26
  • The IR will have 280 gaming tables and 1,260 gaming machines
    • These will add 20% to table capacity and 15% to gaming machine capacity in Entertainment City
  • Travellers will operate the IR instead of SUN
BANKS
Asset quality metrics steady in June, but...

The Philippine banking sector’s asset quality seemed stable in June. (As a reminder, we use loans excluding interbank loans (IBL) and reverse repos (RRP) to remove the “noise” in the data, as the IBL/RRP balances fluctuate widely on a monthly basis.)

 

NPL ratio (ex-IBL/RRP) came in at 3.56%, about 2bps lower MoM from the 3.58% in May. In nominal terms, NPLs were up 0.5% MoM and 5.5% YoY to P530.1bn. Past Due (PD) ratio though was up 3bps MoM to 4.50% from 4.47% in May, as the PHP value of PDs increased 1.7% MoM. Restructured Loans (RLs) improved to 2.09%, 4bps lower MoM. Meanwhile, NPL Cover increased slightly to 76.4% from 75.8% in May.

 

Note, though, that the NPL and PD figures are period-end, and do not take into account write-offs during the period. This masks the new NPL formation, which is more relevant. This was in full display in 2Q, where nearly all banks that have reported thus far showed sharply higher credit costs / provision expense in 2Q5 compared to 1Q25 and to 2Q24. That said, the increase was due largely to the shift towards higher-risk / higher-margin consumer loans. Despite the higher provisions, bank earnings were still up YoY, suggesting better risk-adjusted returns.

 

Loan growth (ex-IBL/RRP) accelerated to 12.1% YoY, up from 11.7% in May and from 11.2% in April. (In contrast, the reported loan growth slowed sharply to 10.5% due to the sharply lower IBL and RRP balances YoY). Industry LDRs dipped to 72.1% from 73.4% the previous month.

 

By bank type, larger universal/commercial banks (UKBs) saw NPLs down 3bps MoM, but PDs inched up 2bps MoM. Thrift banks (TBs) posted huge improvements in both ratios, with NPL ratios down 47bps MoM and PD ratios down 85bps. Meanwhile, Digibanks’ ratios deteriorated MoM, as NPLs jumped 130bps to 11.1% and PDs up 128bps.

 

 

BANKS/DIGITAL FINANCE
Apple Pay / Google Pay to operate in PH soon?

Last week, at a “press chat”, Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) Deputy Governor Mamerto Tangonan said that the BSP had cleared the way for Apple Pay and Google Pay to operate in the Philippines. To date, NFC-based phone-tap payment options are not available in the Philippines. (I, for example, cannot upload my Philippine credit cards onto Apple Pay, even for use abroad.)

 

The major bone of contention was this: are Apple Pay and Google Pay considered “operating payment systems” (OPSs)? Essentially, are they like e-wallets, that hold users’ / customers’ money? According to DG Tangonan, the BSP has determined that they are NOT OPSs, as they merely process / execute payment credentials. Thus, they do not need to register separately with the BSP as regulator.

 

Allowing Apple Pay / Google Pay NFC could make payments much more convenient, and could further encourage broader digital adoption of payments.

 

For Filipinos, credit card penetration is quite low. But if wallets like GCash, Maya, Shopee Pay, Grab Pay, etc are allowed on the phone makers’ respective OSs, it would vastly improve speed of payments, without having to open the apps. This is crucial especially as the BSP and Department of Transportation (DOTr) are working on inter-operable payment system for all modes of public transportation. At the moment, paying via the apps can be a bit time consuming, even with QR adoption.

 

For tourists, the convenience advantage would be more obvious, with the ability to use their phones to pay without having to whip out their credit cards, or cash.

 

According to the BSP, it is now up to the individual financial service providers (banks, wallets, etc) to negotiate with Apple and Google.

CONGLOS
DMCI Mining secures 25-year mining rights in Palawan
  • DMCI Mining, through its wholly-owned unit Berong Nickel Corp., secured a mineral production sharing agreement (MPSA) for its Long Point property in Palawan
    • MPSA covers 2,100 hectares and is valid for 25 years (renewable for another 25 years)
  • Production at Long Point is set to begin in October
  • DMCI Mining expects to ramp-up nickel production to 2.5-3mn WMT in 2026 from 1.8mn WMT this year
  • DMCI Mining is a wholly-owned unit of DMCI Holdings (DMC PM) and accounts for 8% of profits
PROPERTY
Redevelopment of SM Megamall to be completed in 2027-2029
  • Steven Tan, Head of SM Prime’s mall business, said that the P7bn redevelopment of SM Megamall will be completed between 2027 and 2029
  • The mall is currently undergoing redevelopment in phases
  • Among the changes is the right-sizing of cinemas
    • This will add about 20,000sqm to leasable floor area
  • Megamall will also feature a new Megatrade Hall, a redesigned food court, virtual golf, as well as upgraded common areas and restrooms
  • It will also soon welcome the Pop Mart’s first full scale megastore
  • There will also be an additional 1,600 parking slots
  • Megamall has a gross floor area of about 500,000sqm
  • SMPH is trading at 44% discount to NAV, 1.5X FY25E P/B, and 15.0X FY25E P/E
MACRO
Dept. of Agriculture seeks rice tariffication law amendment before next harvest in March
  • The Department of Agriculture (DA) is pushing for amendments to the Rice Tariffication Law (RTL) for better protection of farmers by reauthorizing the National Food Authority (NFA) power to sell affordable rice directly to the public as well as possibly implementing a floor price on palay (unmilled rice)
  • Laurel noted that House Bill No. 1 (Rice Industry and Consumer Empowerment [RICE] Act) which has been filed by House Speaker Martin Romualdez, "encapsulates the revisions sought by the DA"
  • The target date for the enactment of the proposed amendments is before the start of the next rice Harvest, which begins March next year
